subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Capstone: Adult Lifetime Movement Plan and Defense
essentialQuestion: What is the plan I would still be running in a year, and can I defend every part of it?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of integrating four years of evidence into one working plan in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe stating the reasoning behind each element using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply the access, cost, and time plan that makes it real in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving the review points and the conditions that trigger revision; correct it and explain why.
Connect defending the plan under questioning with revising after critique without abandoning the plan and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Present the adult lifetime movement plan to one trusted adult, defend every element with reasoning and evidence from the four-year portfolio, and produce a revised final version.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The defense may be spoken one-to-one, written, presented as annotated slides, or delivered as a conversation. No public presentation, recording, or audience is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
